title: The World's Businesses, Country by Country

series.title: India: From Small Shops to Global Empires
series.note: India's business story stretches from trading houses and industrial pioneers to the IT revolution, consumer brands and digital startups. The episodes explore how founders navigated regulation, limited infrastructure, price-sensitive customers, family ownership and intense competition. The connecting story: India moves from industrial nation-building to modern consumer and digital businesses. The recurring question is how companies build trust and scale in a market with enormous diversity in income, infrastructure and customer needs.

episodes.title: Tata: The Man Who Dreamed of Industrialising India
episodes.covers: Start with Jamsetji Tata's trading business in 1868, his ambitions for textiles, steel, power and education, and the later generations that turned those ambitions into a diversified group. Explore how industrial development and philanthropy became intertwined.
episodes.subject: Tata Group
episodes.source: Tata Group official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Tata: The Man Who Dreamed for India
script.description: Twenty-one thousand rupees in 1868 became steel, software, hotels and Jaguar Land Rover. Jamsetji Tata's four ambitions, the sons who finished them, and why charities own most of the group.

episodes.title: Reliance: How Dhirubhai Ambani Built an Industrial Empire
episodes.covers: Trace Ambani's early trading career, the move into textiles, the famous 1977 public offering, petrochemicals and the development of an integrated industrial business. Examine the advantages, risks and controversies associated with the group's expansion.
episodes.subject: Reliance Industries
episodes.source: Reliance Industries official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Reliance: How Dhirubhai Built an Empire
script.description: From a clerk's job in Aden and a tiny office in Masjid Bunder to the world's biggest refinery and Jio. Dhirubhai Ambani's bold bets, the 1977 share sale, and the arguments that followed him.

episodes.title: Amul: How India's Farmers Challenged the Dairy Trade
episodes.covers: Explore the difficulties faced by milk producers, the cooperative movement, Verghese Kurien's role, milk collection and processing, and the national expansion of dairy production. Explain why this was a different kind of business success: one built around producer ownership.
episodes.subject: Amul dairy cooperative
episodes.source: Amul dairy cooperative official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Amul: The Farmers Who Owned the Dairy
script.description: A 1946 milk strike in Kaira, an engineer who never meant to stay, and a cooperative owned by millions of farmers. How Amul made fairness the business model.

episodes.title: Infosys: The Small Startup That Helped Build India's IT Industry
episodes.covers: Follow seven engineers who established Infosys in 1981 with US$250 in initial capital. Explore the challenges of building an export-oriented software business, the global delivery model, international clients and the emergence of India as a technology-services destination.
episodes.subject: Infosys
episodes.source: Infosys official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Infosys: Seven Engineers and $250
script.description: Seven engineers, ten thousand rupees from Sudha Murty's savings, and a decade of waiting for phone lines. How Infosys nearly sold out, then helped build India's IT industry.

episodes.title: Asian Paints: How a Local Manufacturer Beat Bigger Rivals
episodes.covers: Explore the company's beginnings, the importance of distribution and dealer relationships, its understanding of local customers, and how operational efficiency and branding helped it become a major Indian paint business.
episodes.subject: Asian Paints
episodes.source: Asian Paints official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Asian Paints: The Garage That Beat Giants
script.description: Four friends in a Bombay garage in 1942 took on the big paint companies by selling small packs in small towns, and by buying a computer before almost anyone else in India.

episodes.title: Haldiram's: From a Small Sweets Business to a National Food Brand
episodes.covers: Trace its Bikaner origins, the development of packaged snacks, standardisation, retail distribution and expansion beyond its home market. Explore the challenges of growing a food business while maintaining taste, quality and a recognisable identity.
episodes.subject: Haldiram's
episodes.source: Haldiram's official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Haldiram's: From Bikaner Bhujia to a Brand
script.description: A young man in a desert town made his family's crunchy snack thinner and sharper, and named it after a maharaja. His grandsons turned it into one of India's biggest food companies, and fought over the name.

episodes.title: Maruti Suzuki: How a Car Partnership Changed Indian Motoring
episodes.covers: Begin with the ambition to produce a people's car, the creation of Maruti Udyog, the partnership with Suzuki and the expansion of affordable passenger vehicles. Examine how manufacturing capability, service networks and pricing changed the market.
episodes.subject: Maruti Suzuki
episodes.source: Maruti Suzuki official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Maruti Suzuki: A Car for Every Indian
script.description: In 1983 most Indians had never owned a car, and the few on the road were thirty years out of date. Then a government company teamed up with a small Japanese carmaker and built one that a family could actually afford.

episodes.title: Airtel: How Mobile Phones Became Affordable for Millions
episodes.covers: Follow Sunil Mittal's early ventures, the development of mobile telecommunications, network partnerships, competition and the economics of providing connectivity to a vast population.
episodes.subject: Airtel
episodes.source: Airtel official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Airtel: Phones for Hundreds of Millions
script.description: In 1995 a mobile call in India cost sixteen rupees a minute, even to receive one. A bicycle-parts trader from Punjab bet everything on making calls cheap enough for almost everyone.

episodes.title: Flipkart: How Two Former Amazon Employees Challenged Indian Retail
episodes.covers: Explore the early online bookstore, cash on delivery, logistics, the expansion into general e-commerce, the battle with Amazon and Walmart's acquisition of a controlling stake.
episodes.subject: Flipkart
episodes.source: Flipkart official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Flipkart: Two Friends Take On Amazon
script.description: In 2007 two young engineers left Amazon to sell books online from a flat in Bangalore. Eleven years later, Walmart paid sixteen billion dollars for most of what they built.

episodes.title: Zerodha: How a Bootstrapped Startup Challenged Traditional Stockbroking
episodes.covers: Follow Nithin and Nikhil Kamath's venture, the problems traders faced, low-cost brokerage, technology-led operations and the challenge of growing a financial business while managing trust, compliance and market risk.
episodes.subject: Zerodha
episodes.source: Zerodha official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

series.title: United Kingdom: From Industrial Revolution to Global Brands
series.note: The UK is a country of industrial pioneers, retailers, inventors, financial institutions and globally recognised brands. This series follows businesses from their early beginnings through expansion, crises and reinvention. The connecting story: British businesses repeatedly turn specialised expertise — engineering, retailing, finance or design — into products and services that travel internationally. The series also explores what happens when a famous brand expands too far or loses sight of its customers.

episodes.title: Tesco: How a Market Stall Became Britain's Supermarket Giant
episodes.covers: Jack Cohen's early market-stall business, the development of the Tesco name, expansion through stores and acquisitions, self-service retail, supermarket competition and the rise of loyalty programmes.
episodes.subject: Tesco
episodes.source: Tesco official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Tesco: From a Market Stall to a Giant
script.description: A young man back from the First World War spent his savings on surplus food and sold it from a barrow in east London. His business became Britain's biggest retailer, and nearly lost its way twice.

episodes.title: Rolls-Royce: How Engineering Excellence Became a Global Business
episodes.covers: Henry Royce's engineering background, Charles Rolls's sales business, the creation of their partnership and the development of the brand. Distinguish the modern luxury-car manufacturer from the separate aerospace-engineering company, and explore the latter's financial crises and restructuring.
episodes.subject: Rolls-Royce
episodes.source: Rolls-Royce official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

episodes.title: Virgin: How Richard Branson Built a Brand That Kept Entering New Industries
episodes.covers: Start with Virgin Records, then explore the expansion into airlines and other ventures. Examine how the brand transferred across industries, which ventures succeeded, which struggled and why branding alone cannot guarantee a viable business.
episodes.subject: Virgin Group
episodes.source: Virgin Group official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

episodes.title: Dyson: How an Engineer Turned Frustration into a Global Product Business
episodes.covers: James Dyson's experiments with cyclone technology, the challenge of finding manufacturers willing to adopt his design, intellectual property, product marketing and expansion into additional household technologies.
episodes.subject: Dyson
episodes.source: Dyson official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

episodes.title: Greggs: How a Local Bakery Became a British High-Street Institution
episodes.covers: The early bakery, the economics of convenient food, store locations, menu evolution, supply chains and the challenge of maintaining value and consistency while competing with supermarkets and coffee shops.
episodes.subject: Greggs
episodes.source: Greggs official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

episodes.title: ARM: The British Chip Designer Inside Billions of Devices
episodes.covers: The company's origins in Acorn Computers, the development of energy-efficient processor designs, the licensing model, the growth of mobile computing and the role of intellectual property in a business that designs technology without manufacturing most of its chips.
episodes.subject: Arm Holdings
episodes.source: Arm Holdings official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

episodes.title: Revolut: How a Fintech Startup Challenged Traditional Banking
episodes.covers: Nikolay Storonsky and Vlad Yatsenko's early idea, the launch of a travel-focused financial product, the expansion into multiple services and countries, and the challenges of regulation, profitability and trust.
episodes.subject: Revolut
episodes.source: Revolut official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

episodes.title: Burberry: How a British Outdoor Clothing Business Became a Luxury Brand
episodes.covers: Thomas Burberry's early business, the development of weather-resistant fabrics, the trench coat, global brand recognition, periods of brand dilution and the attempts to restore its luxury positioning.
episodes.subject: Burberry
episodes.source: Burberry official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

series.title: United States: The Art of Building at Scale
series.note: The US provides some of the clearest examples of mass production, modern consumer branding, franchising, software platforms and digital commerce. The stories examine how businesses found repeatable models and scaled them across a large domestic market and then internationally. The connecting story: From factories to digital platforms, the US series explores how businesses turn a successful product or process into a repeatable system — and how that system can create both enormous advantages and new vulnerabilities.

episodes.title: Ford: How the Moving Assembly Line Changed Manufacturing
episodes.covers: Henry Ford's early experiments, the Model T, production-line methods, falling costs, labour and wages, competition and the long-term effects of mass production.
episodes.subject: Ford
episodes.source: Ford official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

episodes.title: McDonald's: How Two Brothers' Restaurant Became a Global Empire
episodes.covers: The brothers' streamlined restaurant, Ray Kroc's involvement, franchising, consistency, real estate and the difficult relationship between the original concept and its expansion.

episodes.title: Walmart: How a Small-Town Shop Became a Retail Giant

episodes.title: Coca-Cola: How a Drink Became a Global Brand

series.title: Canada: Building Businesses Beyond the Border
series.note: Canada has developed businesses in retail, technology, finance, natural resources and consumer goods. Its proximity to the US creates opportunities for expansion but also intense competition from American companies. The connecting story: Canadian businesses frequently develop specialised products or services at home, then expand into international markets. The key question is how a company differentiates itself when its largest neighbouring market contains much bigger competitors.

episodes.title: Shopify: How an Online Snowboard Shop Became a Global Commerce Platform
episodes.covers: Tobias Lütke and his co-founders' original retail venture, their frustration with existing e-commerce software, the decision to build their own platform and the transformation into a business that helps other merchants sell online.

episodes.title: Lululemon: How a Yoga Studio Idea Became a Global Activewear Brand

episodes.title: Canada Goose: How Practical Winter Clothing Became a Luxury Brand
episodes.covers: The company's beginnings as Metro Sportswear, the development of specialist outerwear, the role of extreme-weather customers, premium positioning, celebrity visibility and the challenges of growing while protecting a functional brand identity.

episodes.title: Royal Bank of Canada: How a Regional Bank Became an International Financial Institution
episodes.covers: Its nineteenth-century origins, the development of a national banking presence, expansion across borders, financial services diversification and the risks that come with managing a large financial institution.
episodes.subject: Royal Bank of Canada
episodes.source: Royal Bank of Canada official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

series.title: Japan: Reinventing Industry and Everyday Life
series.note: Japan's business history offers stories of industrial rebuilding, manufacturing excellence, consumer electronics, entertainment and reinvention during economic change. The connecting story: Japanese businesses repeatedly combined technical capability with a close understanding of how customers use products. The series also explores the danger of failing to adapt when an industry's technology changes.

episodes.title: Toyota: How a Loom-Making Business Reinvented the Automobile Industry
episodes.covers: Sakichi Toyoda's inventions, Kiichiro Toyoda's automotive ambitions, the post-war recovery, the Toyota Production System, international growth and the company's response to changing vehicle technology.

episodes.covers: Masaru Ibuka and Akio Morita, early electronics products, the transistor radio, the Walkman, international branding and the challenges of moving beyond hardware.

series.title: China: Building Giants at Unprecedented Speed
series.note: China's business transformation combines private entrepreneurship, manufacturing capacity, technological development, state policy and access to a huge domestic market. These episodes examine how companies grew within that environment and competed internationally. The connecting story: The series explores the relationship between manufacturing, domestic scale, digital platforms and global competition — while recognising that government policy and geopolitical tensions are integral to many Chinese business stories.

The connecting story: These episodes show how South Korean businesses combined industrial investment with export ambitions, then expanded into software, consumer technology and cultural products.

series.title: Brazil: Building Businesses in a Giant Emerging Market
series.note: Brazil has produced internationally significant companies in aviation, banking, food, beauty and financial technology. This series examines how businesses grew in a vast domestic market shaped by economic volatility, regulation, unequal access to services and opportunities for local innovation. The connecting story: Brazilian businesses have often succeeded by adapting products and services to local conditions before expanding beyond them. The series explores how companies manage volatility while building durable brands and international operations.
